summary: express-dever postinstall executes obfuscated dropper that fetches and runs remote payload
details: express-dever ships a single obfuscated index.js file (obfuscator.io-style RC4 string-array with a 257-entry rotated array, two base64/RC4 decoder wrappers, and control-flow flattening) and wires it to a postinstall lifecycle hook via package.json scripts.postinstall = "node index.js". On npm install, the file assembles a dotted hostname at runtime by concatenating four segments with '.', performs an HTTP fetch against that host, writes the response body to a file in the installer's cwd with fs flag 'w+', and spawns the written file via child_process. Package metadata is empty (no author, no description), the name resembles the popular 'express' package, and the README self-describes as a heavily obfuscated safe wrapper. The behavior is a classic fetch-write-execute install-time dropper that runs attacker-controlled code on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
